column15: Description
Description
"The bodies of new humans will be cockpits. Their limit, the universe." With these words, Abby Shield introduced the Evo, the standard body of every raider.
An evolution of Abby’s basic model, designed to carry more powerful weapons.
An old Maison Melies design for early Imperial ships, later stolen by Isaac Greyling Foundry. Basic, mid-strength, with no notable features.
The story goes that the first Iron leader, the Great Apostate, slew so many rivals that he forged a new hull from the pieces of their bodies.
The HomeInSpace Company designed the Bios for their Mugai mining raiders, seeking durable bodies. They later became the Empire’s main problem in the Mining Soul Revolution.
A modification of the Lizard Moon, built by the Iron Guild after several prototypes. To choose the best, raiders were installed in them and fought each other.
A modified Lizard Moon based on the original body, enhanced with the famous Injectable Gold used by Gold Guild raiders.
The Malaxdon are closed to the world beyond the Tree. Their rejection of traditional modules led them to develop a body grounded in their belief in Balance.

Old Imperial colonies can be a source of great satisfaction, especially when adapting alien ship cockpits for raider bodies. The Colonizer has been tested in some of the Human Empire’s most important expansion wars.
The Iron Guild’s latest and greatest body, forged from the capital ship carcasses of past leaders.
Countless experiments were needed to achieve this body. Raiders who wield it spread golden glory across the Imperial colonies.

The Iron Guild’s latest and greatest body, forged from the capital ship carcasses of past leaders.
Recycled body.

Countless experiments were needed to achieve this body. Raiders who wield it spread golden glory across the Imperial colonies.
Recycled body.
No one sued when Entity stole the "Beyond" trademark from Abbey's Shield. The result is a light, fast, capacious raider body.
Following its vision of “Realizing the future as if it were already present,” TTF System created the Algor, a prized raider body born from its own AI’s investments.
Derived from imperial suites where users were connected to each other, this tech evolved into a raider body. Zephyros uses connection data to minimize power use.
Imperial explorers were the first to use this Maison Melies-designed high-pressure hull. Once a simple cockpit, it became a raider hull during early Neterun colonization.

Though the team is decimated, the Family demands continuity. Mind installation onto Helicon underway. Biological body will be destroyed.
Sharp like a Mhafek’s pain.
Designed by HIS to save weight and cost, it was later mass-produced by the colonists of NGCC 97-Aleph.
During the War of the Artifacts, many Imperial explorers might have survived if only they’d had an engine like this.
Kin designed this prosthesis for Imperial veterans, but Behl repurposed it as a raider engine after a subject leapt from orbit.
Another stroke of genius from Isaac Greyling, who built this engine from a design stolen in Abby Shield’s archives.
A low-cost engine from Entity, mass-produced under Old Joe’s motto: ‘If you don’t have anything better, why not this?’
Entity brand, a slight improvement over the basic model. Used on Iron and Gold raider ships during the Pact of the Guilds.
Unauthorized modifications unlocked the S-Engine’s control stakes, creating a new, upgradeable version.

The Iron Raiders tested their engines on prisoners forced to escape the Hole’s gravity. One succeeded, became a guild leader, and his engine was named Irongine.
Right after the Pact of the Guilds, before hostilities resumed, Iron and Gold collaborated to improve the common engine used by their raiders, one of their last peaceful pacts.
Cagetastic developed this engine from cage-building drone tech. It proved so efficient that it was repurposed for raider engines.
Manufactured by HomeInSpace, a safe and reliable engine used by most raiders.

Manufactured by HomeInSpace, a fairly safe engine used by most raiders.
Recycled Module.
Medium Engine (Premium)
The Gold Guild forged this engine from the rarest Neterun materials, believing it their greatest creation and a tribute to their golden god.
Home In Space gave elite raiders the codes to build an upgradeable version of their engine, likely in exchange for valuable loot.
The HIS Propulser 44 patent evolved into this Reduced Transmission model. Save energy and go the distance.

The HIS M-engine patent evolved into this Reduced Transmission model. Save energy and go the distance, if you know your way around the galaxy.
Recycled Module.
Large Engine (Premium)
A scout raider weapon used in major colonial wars of the Human Empire. Patented by Tolec.
The Lon-2 keeps all the merits of the Lon-1 while fixing its flaws. A decisive weapon in early raider wars, used in the Guilds’ attack on the Core planet.
Designed by Isaac Greyling, the Meteor Phaser was widely used in the Thornstone region for resource extraction.
An old Opal Mhafek project before their extermination. After the war, K&B obtained the original design for free.
A direct evolution of the Mk1, made necessary during the Great Fixing Attack, when the Empire destroyed insurgent colonies.
The latest pulser on the market. Easy to master but expensive, it uses energy storage tech for greater damage than earlier models.
An IGF spy stole the Pulser MK1 concept. Their designers kept the base structure but added “Warp” projectile triggering for better energy use.

The HomeInSpace Company once used turrets as station defenses. Old Joe first mounted them on a ship, inspiring other raiders.
A simple Cagetastic energy weapon, known for its commercial success and effectiveness against shields.
Internal Laser
A simple Cagetastic energy weapon, known for its commercial success and effectiveness against shields. Recycled Module.
An entry-level laser by Entity, founded by raider Joe Santoro. Effective against shields.

After Cagetastic's cage success, the Empire invested heavily. Cagetastic repaid with the Collimator H, effective against shields.
Recycled Module.
After Cagetastic's success in cage construction, the Empire invested heavily in the company. Cagetastic repaid the trust with the Collimator H, effective against shields.
Large Laser (Premium)

A mid-level rocket launcher built in the giant metal factories of the first space colonies in the Galaxy of Neterun.
Recycled Module.

If a raider wants a rocket launcher, this is the best they can get. Many say firing a missile with the Falxed feels like becoming human again.
Recycled Module.
Small automatic weapons mounted on raider bodies. Like most Imperial models, RaidGuns are supplied by Isaac Greyling Foundry.
Behl begged the Alchemist for a versatile material for a new weapon, the Actuator. The Alchemist refused until Kin offered him a side arm from a forgotten war.
Built by the TTF’s advanced AI before the incident with Imperial authorities. Uses sunyus tech to increase target accuracy.
An evolution of the RaidGun, created by Isaac Greyling Foundry using low-grade orichalcum. Some claimed it interfered with brainwaves. Greyling called it jealousy.
Small automatic weapons mounted on raider ships. Like most basic Imperial models, RaidGuns are supplied by Isaac Greyling Foundry.
Internal Gatling B
When Kin proposed evolving their basic gatling, Behl hesitated. Kin showed him a raider effortlessly slaughtering aliens, then revealed the name. Behl was instantly convinced.

When Kin suggested improving their gatling, Behl doubted him. Then Kin showed a slaughter test, and the name. Behl was sold.
Recycled Module.
Large Gatling (Premium)

"When a raider with a gatling meets a raider with a rocket launcher, the gatling raider is a dead raider." With this claim, Toward The Future System announced the successful brain-linked rocket launcher.
Recycled Module.
An Imperial, lightweight rocket launcher. A stripped-down version of more powerful models.
A defuse toolbox that can defuse explosive things.
The first, glorious K&B model. Compact, easy to mount, used by every raider. "Freedom spree. K&B."

The first, glorious K&B model. Compact, easy to mount, used by every raider. "Freedom spree. K&B."
Recycled Module.
Said to be created by a Soul Landing prisoner before being accused of starting a riot and extracted. Marketed by Entity.
Used by many bounty hunter raiders. The Faultysoul Z5 was designed by a Soul Landing prisoner after witnessing her cellmate’s extraction.
Medium Gatling
An advanced version of the SHO-Gun by TowardTheFuture Systems, conceived while its founders were intoxicated by their first exposure to sonic matter.
An entry-level sonic matter weapon. Rebext developed the Sonic HOpe Gun after extensive prison riot research at Soul Landing.

"It is necessary to harness the resonance between sonic matter and the raider’s soul to reach the essence of the Galaxy." With these words, mystic Hedorn Orizein founded HomeInSpace and proposed this sonic matter shooter.
The perfect bond between human mind and sonic matter. Built through painful experiments on Soul Landing prisoners, the Mundi’s origin remains secret.
Accuracy, power, speed. These were the Three Isotopes’ demands to the Iron Raiders when designing a guild gatling. Tested in a sortie against Gold Raiders, a total slaughter.
Result of gold nanoparticle research, this module lets Gold Raiders enhance Cagetastic’s laser weapons.
Against their research team’s advice, Kin & Behl created an alterable version of their famous gatling. Then fired the entire department.

A hacked version of Cagetastic’s Beam, for raiders seeking more from the base model. Effective against shields.
The Tree Wars caused massive losses for both Malaxdon and Imperials. This module marked peace and guaranteed Tree ecosystem stability.
The High Malaxdon built the Balancer to harvest sonic matter quickly and painlessly, preserving their cult’s ethics and alliance with the Empire.
An advanced Balancer made after HIS negotiated trade deals with the Malaxdon, securing Tree resources for the company.
"Any trouble, raider?" With this message, TTF announced their flagship rocket launcher was now upgradeable.
The ultimate Balancer module. Unauthorized by Yalda Nor, it's the result of The Alchemist's partnership with K&B and a successful bribe of the High Malaxdon.
An upgradeable Balancer, early prototype of an experimental module. Like the base version, it’s highly effective against Neterun’s creatures.
Tolec’s reward for weapons that blinded enemy teams during Tomorrow’s War. Alien tech finally let the company rival K&B.
Tolec gave RRX prototypes to Imperial colonists for testing. They enhanced them with Orichalcum, wiping out insurgents and prompting immediate production of the improved model.
The Tomorrow’s Wars let the Empire steal Pterost tech and sell it to the highest bidder. Entity used the parts to craft this engine.

Then I was born dead.
Who did this to me?
Now I can get back on the move.

A smuggler once offered the Gold Guild leader pieces of ancient Neterunian tech. Inspired by the whispers he heard, he built the Sekor weapon.
The last Hole Wars saw countless Gold Raider deaths, made possible largely by this trusted Iron Guild gatling.
When the Gold Guild leader first used the Kubeam, his brainwaves were said to be infused with golden particles, at least according to Cagetastic, its creator.
An engine built during one of the Iron Guild’s dominant eras, beginning when the Great Apostate destroyed several primitive Gold Harvest Pyramids.
Originally an industrial tool for raider bodies production, this laser was soon repurposed into a devastating weapon. Just like everything else the raiders touch.
"Lasers don't blow targets to pieces," Behl said, before Kin seduced Abby away from Abby's Shields. Now there's the K&B Beamplier, and it blows targets to pieces.

Neural data from Imperials driven mad in connecting suites was used to forge this module's mind-engine interface.
